name: Bashan
overview: Bashan is a fertile and productive region located east of the Jordan River and north of the Arnon River, famously known for its fine cattle and dense forests. It was the kingdom of Og, the last of the Rephaim giants, whose iron bedstead symbolized his formidable stature. The land was conquered by Israel under Moses and allotted to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh, marking it as a significant inheritance east of the Jordan. Despite being invaded by foreign kings such as Hazael of Syria, Bashan was retaken by Jehoash, underscoring its strategic and spiritual importance in Israel's history.
